_comment: Canonical join graph the Pharmacy Cost accelerator reasons over. Accelerator-owned and TARGET-AGNOSTIC: endpoints are logical OBJECTS and logical ELEMENT ids (LOGICAL_ID from logical_elements.json), never physical customer tables/columns. Phase-1 discovery instantiates each into a physical row in ACCELERATOR_CORE_RELATIONSHIPS (LEFT_OBJECT/LEFT_COLUMN/RIGHT_OBJECT/RIGHT_COLUMN/JOIN_CONDITION) for the customer's schema. REQUIRED is set MINIMALLY: only joins whose BOTH endpoints are required objects and that a required arm needs. All others stay REQUIRED=false and are present()-gated in the templates (graceful degradation). CARDINALITY hints whether the renderer must de-dup (MANY_TO_MANY / >1 rows-per-key => dedup); the profiled cardinality_profile in config.json overrides it.

relationships.PURPOSE: Enrich each Rx claim line to therapeutic class / GPI / specialty / generic / maintenance. Both endpoints are required objects.
Net-of-rebate spend and rebate yield by class. Absent => net = gross. May instead be a rebate-% column on the claim (element on RX_DRUG_CLAIM, no join).
On/off-formulary leakage, preferred alternative, tier. Formulary often has many rows per NDC => de-dup (see cardinality_profile.PHCLM_NDC__FORMULARY).
Price component of the PVM trend decomposition (MDL_TREND_DRIVERS). Price history is NDC x effective-date; the consuming template selects the applicable period. Absent => PVM collapses to volume+mix.
Attach member / status / service dates to medical (buy-and-bill) drug lines. Absent => those fields must live on MEDICAL_DRUG_LINE and this join is dropped.
Medical drug name / class / ASP / specialty for J-code lines. Required only when MEDICAL_DRUG_LINE is present.
Site-of-care setting / cost tier for specialty-medical. POS may alternatively be on the medical header (MCH_PLACE_OF_SERVICE_CODE).
Enrich member-months with funding arrangement / risk score. Absent => those enrichments are omitted.
Trend-vs-plan KPI and forecast baseline by line of business. Absent => plan/budget comparisons omitted.
